cards.english: Remember this rule!
cards.existing: Exceptions: nouns ending in `-ь` can be either masc or fem – `день` (day, m), `ночь` (night, f). Memorize these. Some `-а` nouns are masc by meaning: `папа`, `дядя`, `мужчина`.

cards.existing: For 'whose?', ask `чей/чья/чьё/чьи?` – same gender/number agreement: `чей это дом?` (whose house is this?).

cards.existing: Use `себя` for the object position; use the reflexive suffix `-ся` if the verb has a reflexive form: `мыться` (wash oneself) vs `мыть себя` (which sounds odd).

cards.existing: Possessives agree with the owned noun: `мой брат` (m), `моя сестра` (f), `моё окно` (n), `мои книги` (pl). Endings shift by gender, number, case.

cards.existing: Different subjects → `чтобы (chtoby) + past tense`: `Я хочу, чтобы ты пришёл` (I want you to come – literally 'that you came'). Past tense even though hypothetical.

cards.target: Не торопитесь с решением, у вас ещё есть время.

cards.target: Найди ошибку в этом тексте, она где-то в начале.

cards.existing: Possessives agree with the owned noun: `мой брат` (m), `моя сестра` (f), `моё окно` (n), `мои книги` (pl). Endings shift by gender, number, case.

cards.existing: Past tense verbs also agree with the subject's gender: `он читал` (on chital) (m), `она читала` (f), `оно читало` (n). Adjectives, pronouns, and past verbs – all visibly gendered.

cards.existing: `Его/её/их` (his/her/their) DON'T change – they're fixed forms regardless of what's owned. `Его дом`, `его машина`, `его книги` – all `его`.

cards.existing: Possessives precede the noun: `мой дом` (moy dom), not `дом мой`. Putting it after sounds emphatic or poetic.

cards.existing: `Чтобы` (Chtoby) always introduces purpose or desire. After verbs of wanting/asking/ordering with a different subject in the subordinate clause, it's required.
